site.name: Grant County Mine
site.componentDetail: Historic hard-rock mine near Caribou recorded by USGS MRDS as a past producer of gold, lead, and silver and preserved as a named mine on USGS-derived topographic mapping.
overview: The Grant County Mine is a historic hard-rock property in the Caribou mining area of Boulder County. Federal mineral-resource records classify it as a past producer associated with gold, lead, and silver.

The mine was attracting attention by late 1882, when a Caribou ore specimen from the Grant County was reported in the Rocky Mountain News and compared favorably with prominent Colorado ore of the period.

timeline.text: A December report in the Rocky Mountain News described a noteworthy ore specimen from the Grant County Mine at Caribou, showing that the property was active and attracting attention during the district's nineteenth-century mining era.
Federal mineral-resource records preserved the Grant County as a past-producing Boulder County mine with gold, lead, and silver commodities.
USGS-derived topographic and geographic-name datasets continue to identify Grant County Mine as a distinct named mine feature near Caribou.

moreHistory: The name refers to the mine property, not to Grant County, Colorado; the site is in Boulder County near the historic Caribou mining district.
Available sources support a meaningful identification and production context, but they do not establish a complete operator history, production total, or the condition of surviving workings.
The mapped point is a historic site reference, not a safe entrance or an assurance of public access. Visitors should respect property boundaries and never enter mine openings.
